rows.en: <operator(1040,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Faye<ce()>. Is <color(5)>Berkt<ce()> really going to show up? I wonder if it was right to come back here...
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)>All we can do is trust our own call.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>I know that, but... Something's still nagging at me.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>If he knows we're after the <color(5)>Shin Dragon<ce()>, I'd think he'd be on guard, too.
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)>However he comes at us, what matters is the mission in front of us. Right now we need to focus on the <color(5)>Shin Dragon<ce()>.
<operator(19020,1)><speed(2)><color(5)>Saotome<ce()>... Because of the <color(5)>Shin Dragon<ce()> he built, so many of our comrades died.
<operator(19020,1)><speed(2)>I will never... forgive him.
<operator(19030,1)><speed(2)>But man, can we really take down a monster like that?
<operator(19020,1)><speed(2)>Dad used to say it. Once Getter has you in its grip, there's no escaping that fate.
rows.notes: 'Oyaji' (dad/pop) - Kei's adoptive father is Benkei per glossary; rendered as 'Dad'.

rows.en: <operator(19020,1)><speed(2)>But he also said Getter gives you infinite power in return.
<operator(19010,1)><speed(2)>That's right... have faith.
<operator(23010,1)><speed(2)>They say <color(4)>Hayato<ce()> used to be a legendary pilot... is that true?
rows.notes: '-san' on Hayato dropped, matching corpus convention (see 4004463 review).

rows.en: <operator(21020,1)><speed(2)>Talk about the Getter Team, and I hear they were scary enough to make any monster turn tail and run.
<operator(21020,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Jin<ce()> was that Getter's pilot - as famous as <color(4)>Ryoma Nagare<ce()>, <color(4)>Benkei Kuruma<ce()>, and <color(4)>Musashi Tomoe<ce()>.
rows.notes: Compressed 'there was no one who didn't know his name' to 'as famous as' to fit the limit; '神' rendered 'Jin' (Hayato Jin's surname, used formally here alongside the other three legends).

rows.en: <operator(21020,1)><speed(2)>All of them fought through the Moon Invader War and came to be called heroes.
rows.notes: 'Moon Invader War' per locked provisional name in encyclopedia_021_b.json.

rows.en: <operator(19050,1)><speed(2)>But 13 years ago, in the Deuteron Missile incident, <color(4)>Musashi<ce()> died and <color(4)>Ryoma<ce()> went missing.
<operator(19020,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Ryoma<ce()>... he still hasn't been found?
<operator(19050,1)><speed(2)>...Enough talk. Let's move out.
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Barrel<ce()>... Is <color(5)>Berkt<ce()> bothering you?
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>Yeah... Why he knows me... I want to find that out.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>More than that, he's trying to do something awful. I have to stop him regardless.
<operator(1060,2)><speed(2)>...You've toughened up a lot in such a short time. That's a boy for you.
rows.notes: 'That's a boy for you' echoes the idiom shape used for the same line 'saizuga otoko no ko' in 4004433 1/23 (not copied, independently natural).

rows.en: <operator(23020,1)><speed(2)>This kid again... <color(4)>Nirvash<ce()>'s emotions are running high.
rows.notes: 'kono ko' (this child) = Eureka's pet name for Nirvash; kept as 'this kid'.

rows.en: <operator(23010,1)><speed(2)>Is <color(4)>Nirvash<ce()> sensing something from the <color(5)>Invaders<ce()>?
rows.notes: 'Invaders' (Getter Robo antagonist race) per locked encyclopedia term; color(5) in source matches faction color.

rows.en: <operator(19020,1)><speed(2)>We have the power of Getter.
<operator(19030,1)><speed(2)>Yeah... If the three of us combine our strength, Getter should be invincible.
<operator(19010,1)><speed(2)>That's right, we unite as one. Getter will always answer us.

'-san' on Hayato dropped, matching corpus convention (see 4004463 review).

checked_decisions: 0/24-28 Kei/Gai/Go: 'he' for Saotome (0/24) and for Oyaji/Benkei (0/27-28) both resolve correctly per character_names_021 (Saotome male, Benkei male); 'Dad' for 'oyaji' fits Kei's tomboyish register. Accepted.
0/30 '-san' dropped on Hayato: consistent with corpus convention. Accepted.

0/32 'Jin' + compression of 'sono na wo shiranu mono wa nakatta' to 'as famous as': source lists Jin (surname of Hayato Jin, glossary entry 68) alongside Ryoma Nagare, Benkei Kuruma and Musashi Tomoe as the four Getter Team legends; compression keeps that meaning and the fit. Accepted.
0/33 'Moon Invader War' and 0/34 'Deuteron Missile': verified verbatim against the locked terms in encyclopedia_021_b.json (Musashi Tomoe / Deuteron Missile / Moon Invader War entries). Accepted.
1/22 'That's a boy for you' for 'saizuga otoko no ko': natural idiom, independently arrived at; Barrel is male per glossary so the line is correctly addressed. Accepted.
1/59 'kono ko' -> 'this kid' (Eureka's pet name for Nirvash) and 1/60 'Invaders' (locked Getter antagonist term, color(5) tag matches faction color): both accepted.

Checked every row's speaker id against speaker_lookup.py and character_names_021/glossary.json for gender and role; no mismatches found (e.g. 'he' correctly used for Saotome, Ryoma, Berkt; 'she'/gender-neutral correctly avoided elsewhere).
Scanned all 27 rows for lowercase j/q outside locked names: none found.
Re-ran the console check: all <...> commands identical and in source order, no newlines, ASCII only, all visible text <=120 chars, no bare %.
remaining_uncertainties: 1/19 'Is Berkt bothering you?' renders the same 'ki ni natteiru' construction that 4004543 0/28 renders as 'Is Berkt on your mind?'. Both are valid readings ('bothering'='weighing on your mind' is idiomatic here, not an added negative), but the two scenes now differ in phrasing for a near-identical line; left as a stylistic note, not fixed.
